complexity.notes: Stray print(a) debug line should be removed, and the loop variable i is unused (for _ in range(...) reads better). The true cost is Theta((log n)^2) multiplications — the benchmark model clamps this to n^0.5, the tightest expressible form. A faster O(log n) approach exists: ||standard binary exponentiation, squaring the base and halving the exponent in a single pass instead of recursing on the remainder||, because this version recomputes all lower squarings at every recursion level.
complexity.summary: Recursive exponentiation: squares x up to the largest power of two not exceeding n, then multiplies by the recursive result for the remaining exponent, handling negative n via the reciprocal. Each recursion level redoes its squarings from scratch, so the total number of multiplications is O((log n)^2).
